vahan portal. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 13 
CHAPTER–III 
THE RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH 
THE COMMITTEE HAS NOT ACCEPTED THE REPLIES OF THE 
MINISTRY 
 
Recommendation/ Observation 
24.  The Committee notes that India being the fifth largest automobile market in 
the world, imports crude oil from outside to cover 80% of its transport fossil fuel, 
thereby draining public exchequer and also increasing pollution from traditional 
Internal Combustion Engine Vehicles is at alarming levels. The Committee further 
notes that India‟s EV Ecosystem is still at a nascent stage, as compared to several 
other countries in the world. Therefore, the need of the hour is to scale up the 
transition process to electric mobility. The Committee welcomes the decision taken 
by the Govt. of India to switch over to Hybrid & Electric Vehicles to tackle the 
GHG (CO2) emissions from transport sector, helping to reduce crude oil import 
and also be in line with the latest global technology. 
(Para 11) 
Action Taken Replies 
 Adoption of EVs is being promoted through three major policy 
interventions as below:  
(i) In order to make India a global manufacturing hub of Automobile & Auto 
Components a Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for Aut omobile and 
Auto Components was approved on 15th September 2021 with a budgetary outlay 
of Rs. 25,938 crore for a period of five years. Electric Vehicles are covered under 
Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for Automobile and Auto Components. 
(ii) The Government on 12th May, 2021 approved a Production Linked 
Incentive (PLI) scheme for manufacturing of Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) in 
the country in order to bring down prices of battery in the country. Drop in battery 
price will result in cost reduction of electric vehicles. 
(iii) FAME-II, which is being implemented for a period of 5 years w.e.f. 01st 
April, 2019 with a total budgetary support of Rs. 10,000 crores, focusses on 
supporting electrification of public & shared transportation and aims to support, 
through subsidies, 7090 e-Buses, 5 lakh e-3 Wheelers, 55000 e-4 Wheeler 
Passenger Cars and 10 lakhs e-2wheelers.  
 
Further Recommendation/Observation  
 
The Committee notes that the Government on 12th May, 2021  has 
approved a Production Linked Incenti ve (PLI) scheme for manufacturing of 
Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) in the country to bring down prices of 
battery in the country.  The Committee desires to be apprised of the Status 
Report regarding the progress  made as on date in this direction. 
 
 
 

 14 
 
Recommendation/ Observation 
25. The Committee further suggests that similar measures to promote EV 
adoption also be taken in respect of other segments such as e3w & e4w (private 
vehicles). Further all the States should be made aware of the benefits of the FAME 
scheme to encourage consumers to opt for EVs. 
 
(Para 22 (ii)) 
Action Taken Replies 
In e3W and e4W segment, only public transport/commercial vehicles are 
incentivized in order to spread allocated fund to maximum beneficiaries as no of 
user of public transpo rt/commercial vehicle is much more than private people. 
Further, vehicle used for commercial purpose/ public transport are having greater 
visibility. Further, fuel saving and reduction in emission is more in vehicles used 
for commercial/public transport pu rpose as compared to private vehicles.  All 
States/UT have been informed about benefits of the FAME scheme. 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation  
 
The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry that all the states have 
been informed about the FAME scheme.  The Committee recommends that 
the Ministry should organise regular meetings with the States to promote 
manufacturing of EVs, EV components and EV infrastructure. The 
Committee is of the opinion that even though only public 
transport/commercial vehicles in e -3W and e -4 W are being incentivized, 
there was an impending need to promote e -4W (private vehicles) as the basic 
purpose is to reduce dependence on ICE vehicles which are one of the major 
source of pollution. The Committee desires to be apprised of the meas ures 
taken as on date in this direction. 
 
Recommendation/ Observation 
26. The Committee notes that Ministry of Power had launched a nationwide 
campaign “Go Electric” on 19.02.2021 to educate the general public on the 
benefits of e -mobility and Govt. incent ives etc. However, in order to increase the 
awareness about the campaign, the Committee is of the view that advertisements 
should be given in print as well as electronic media in co -ordination with all State 
Governments. Further, efforts should be made to conduct seminars, workshops 
etc. to increase the awareness about the campaign  so that consumers can be 
encouraged to go for EVs, removing apprehensions in their minds about range 
anxiety, charging infrastructure etc. 
(Para 33) 
Action Taken Replies 
Noted. Further, MHI Organized a conference on e -mobility on 4th Dec, 2021 in 
Goa under Chairmanship of Hon’ble Minister of Ministry of Heavy industries 
which was attended by Chief Minister/Goa, Hon’ble MoS/MHI, CEO/NITI 

 15 
Aayog, Secretary Heavy Industries, Transpor t Ministers of States, senior officials 
from States/UTs, senior officials from Central Govt. and CEO/Senior officials 
from Auto Industry. 
 
Recommendation/ Observation 
27. The Committee, therefore, recommends that Government and all other 
stakeholders (espe cially manufacturers) should make use of every feasible 
promotional and advertising platform to highlight the benefits of Electric Vehicles 
and EV technology. Informational campaigns across print and electronic media 
can make a huge impact. In addition to the obvious benefits such as anti -pollution 
and cost -efficiency, busting myths such as battery longevity that surround EV 
usage may also be highlighted. Return on Investment (RoI) and cost of ownership 
benefits of EVs vis a vis conventional Internal Combus tion Engines (ICE) can be 
demonstrated. Customers may also be educated about the various benefits, 
incentives and subsidies offered by the Government such as exemptions of EVs 
from road tax during vehicle registration, discounts offered on purchase of EVs 
etc. 
(Para 87) 
Action Taken Replies 
Noted. MHI Organized a conference on e -mobility on 4th Dec, 2021 in Goa under 
Chairmanship of Hon’ble Minister of Ministry of Heavy industries which was 
joined by Chief Minister/Goa, Hon’ble MoS/MHI, CEO/NITI Aayog, Secr etary 
Heavy Industries, Transport Ministers of States, senior officials from States/UTs, 
senior officials from Central Govt. and CEO/Senior officials from Auto Industry. 
  
Ministry of Power had launched a nationwide campaign "Go Electric" on 
19.02.2021 to educate the general public on the benefits of e -mobility and Govt. 
incentives etc. 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation (for Para 33 and Para 87) 
  
The Committee appreciates the efforts made by the Ministry  of Heavy 
Industries and Ministry of Power  to promo te e -mobility in the country . 
However, in order to fast track the transition to e -mobility, the Committee is 
of the opinion that more initiatives should be taken to spread awareness , 
especially amongst the  owners of those vehicles  with less than  1 year  life, 
about the incentives, subsidie s, benefits of Electric Vehicles  vis-a-vis ICE 
vehicles and remove the apprehensions regarding charging, durability and 
safety of the EVs through SMS/ emails, advertising platforms such as audio, 
visual, print and social me dia. The Committee may be apprised of the 
awareness campaigns organised to educate the consumers about the benefits 
of e-mobility. 
 
 
 

 16 
 
Recommendation/ Observation 
28. The Committee notes that the tariff applicable for domestic consumption 
shall be made app licable for domestic charging, whereas for Public Charging 
Station (PCS) provision a separate metering arrangement shall be made for 
subsidized tariff.  The tariff on domestic consumption is charged on slab basis and 
the consumption of units over and above the fixed quota used for EV charging, are 
charged at a high rate resulting in high electricity bill which is likely to 
discourage consumers for opting EVs. The Committee, therefore, recommends that 
as in the case of Public Charging Station, a sub -meter or  separate meter 
arrangements may be installed for billing the charging point used exclusively for 
EV charging by domestic consumers to keep the electricity bill affordable to 
encourage potential buyers to go for EVs. 
(Para 37) 
Action Taken Replies 
Ministry of Power (MoP) has issued "Charging Infrastructure for Electric Vehicles 
(EV) — the Revised Guidelines and Standards" on 14.01.2022.  
  
As per clause 7.2 of the guidelines "The tariff applicable for domestic 
consumption shall be applicable for domestic charging." 
  
As per clause 7.3 of the revised guidelines:  
"The separate metering arrangement shall be made for PCS so that consumption 
may be recorded and billed as per applicable tariff for EV charging stations." 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation  
The Co mmittee reiterates  that subsidized tariff  for consumption of 
electricity units for EV charging could play a significant role in incentivising 
the consumers to opt for EVs over ICE vehicles. The Committee recommends  
that necessary guidelines should be issue d by MHI to Ministry of Power so as 
to ensure that similar to Public Charging System  (PCS), a separate metering 
arrangement with subsidized tariff shall be made for domestic charging of 
EVs.  
 
Recommendation/ Observation 
29. The Committee notes that curren tly, Scrapping industry in India is 
unorganized and not environment -friendly. Further, the existing scrapping cycle 
has a low recovery percentage in India, which is about 70 -75%, while global 
benchmarks for recovery from scrapped vehicle are in the range o f      85 -95%. 
This not only leads to inefficient resource management, but also         non -
realization of the full value of high -strength steel alloys and recovery of valuable 
rare-earth metals. Enabling vehicle scrapping in a scientific manner by using 
modern technology can enhance value recovery from scrapped vehicles. The 
Committee, therefore, recommends the following measures:- 
 Setting up of Registered Vehicle Scrapping Centres across the country. 

 17 
 Incentivising consumers who opt for EVs and scrap their  old ICE vehicles 
from such registered vehicle scrapping centres. 
(Para 40) 
Action Taken Replies 
The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has formulated the Vehicle 
Scrapping Policy that includes a system of incentives/dis -incentives for creation of 
an ecosystem to phase out older, unfit polluting vehicles. GSR Notification 653 
(E) dated 23.09.2021 provides the Motor Vehicles (Registration and Functions of 
Vehicle Scrapping Facility) Rules, 2021 for establishment of Registered Vehicles 
Scrapping Facility (RVSF). The notification has come into force with effect from 
25th September, 2021. It is also submitted that incentives have been included in 
the policy for purchase of new vehicles against scrapped vehicles: 
• Waiver of registration fee for a new vehicl e purchased against the 
certificate of deposit issued by an RVSF on submission of vehicle for scrapping as 
per GSR 714 (E) dated 4th October 2021. The notification shall come into force 
with effect from 1st April, 2022. 
• Concession in motor vehicle tax upto 25% for non -transport vehicles and 
upto 15% for transport vehicles, for first 15 and 8 years, respectively, for vehicles 
purchased against certificate of deposit as per GSR 720 (E) dated 5th October 
2021. The notification shall come into force with effect from 1st April, 2022. 
• Advisory to vehicle manufacturers for providing a discount of 5% on 
purchase of new vehicle against Certificate of Deposit. 
• Provisions for scientific scrapping to increase recovery rate upto 95% from 
scrapped vehicles. 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
 
The Committee may be apprised of the details of Registered Vehicle 
Scrapping Facility (RVSF) centres setup/likely to be setup in the country and 
the procedure involved in issuing the ‘Certificate of Deposit’ on submission of 
a vehicle for scrapping. Further, safeguards adopted to prevent 
environmental pollution while scrapping old vehicles as well as the steps 
taken to recover valuable rare -earth metals from the scrap ped vehicles may 
also be intimated to the Committee for perusal. Further, the timeline fixed for 
setting up of scrap yards throughout the country to carry out the gargantuan 
task of scrapping all old vehicles may also be intimated to the Committee. 
 
Recommendation/ Observation 
 
30. The Committee is of the opinion tha t there is a strong need to align policies 
across the Center and the State Governments as the difference in the structure and 
quantum of incentives across the Central and State policies, sales of Electric 
Vehicles are not picking up pace across the nation uniformly.  The Committee 
recommends that Government should align the Central and State policies across 
the nation and calibrate them to create a „One India One Policy‟ for early 

 18 
adoption of Electric Mobility in India.  Further, this would give EV manufact urers 
a clear direction to invest and create demand and facilitate mass adoption to EVs 
along the length and breadth of the country. 
(Para 47) 
Action Taken Replies  
As on 18 th Feb, 2022 Eighteen states (Andhra Pradesh, Delhi, Karnataka, Kerala, 
Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Odisha, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, 
Meghalaya, Gujarat, Assam, Goa, Meghalaya, West Bengal and Uttarakhand) 
have approved/notified dedicated EV policies which is aligned with FAME -II and 
EV policies as issued by different Ministries of Central Govt. 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
 
The Committee notes that as on 18th February, 2022 only 18 states have 
approved/ notified dedicated EV policies which are aligned with FAME -II 
and EV policies issued by different Ministries of Cent ral Government. The 
Committee recommends that the Ministry , in order to give further impetus 
to electric mobility, should take up the matter with the remaining States and 
UTs and make efforts so as to avoid any further delay in the approval of EV 
policy.The Committee desires that a status report regarding the same may 
also be furnished. 
 
Recommendation/ Observation 
31. The e3W segment is depressed in demand generation mainly due to 
challenges on affordability. The Committee, recommends that the demand 
incentive slab for e3W from Rs. 10,000/KWh to Rs. 15,000/KWh as done in the 
case of e2W, which will generate demand for e3w and help in creating self -
employment and reduce pollution. 
(Para 58) 
Action Taken Replies  
For increase in sale of e3W, following amendm ents have been brought in the 
FAME notification w.e.from 11th June, 2021: 
  
Aggregation will be the key method for bringing the upfront cost of 3W EV at an 
affordable level and at par with ICE 3 -Wheelers. EESL will aggregate demand for 
3 lakh Electric 3 Wh eelers for multiple user segments. Details will be worked out 
by EESL for implementation. 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation  
 
The Committee appreciates the aggregation strategy adopted by MHI to 
increase the sales of e3W. The Committee further desires  t hat MHI should 
not leave any stone unturned to seize this opportune time to intervene in the 
e3W segment and enhance the demand incentive slab for e3W from Rs. 

 19 
10,000/KWh to Rs. 15,000/ KWh  along with increasing the cap on incentive 
on the cost of e3W vehicle. 
 
Recommendation/ Observation 
32. With the growing per capita income of the country, the purchase of Private 
e4W was expected to go up rapidly since this category has high scope because 
electric car Models available in India are predominantly low cost segment. 
However, lack of incentives to individuals for purchase of e4W has been a big 
roadblock in the consumer‟s mind before opting for purchase of e4W. The 
Committee, therefore, urges that the Government should extend incentives to 
purchase e4W by indiv iduals to boost sales in this category and Fame -II Scheme 
should be modified to this extent, as it is already providing subsidy for commercial 
e4Ws. 
(Para 60) 
Action Taken Replies 
In order to spread allocated fund to maximum beneficiaries as no of user of 
e4W public transport/commercial vehicle is much more than private people. 
Further, e4W vehicle used for commercial purpose/ public transport are having 
greater visibility. Further, fuel saving and reduction in emission is more in 
vehicles used for commerci al/public transport purpose as compared to private 
vehicles. 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation  
 
The Committee desires that along with e4W public 
transport/commercial vehicles, there is an urgent need to incentivize e4W 
private vehicles as public transport fails to provide last mile connectivity and 
consumers are more inclined towards purchasing private vehicle than using 
public vehicles especially in the post pandemic scenerio . The Committee also 
recommends that the MHI should apprise the Committee about  the measures 
taken in this regard. 
 
Recommendation/ Observation 
33. The Committee observes that there is no sufficient R&D Support by the 
Ministry for technological advancement. The spending in India on R&D is point 
less than 1 percent whereas the major e conomies spend around 5 to 6 percent.  
Because of poor funding, India is lagging behind in R&D.  Without sufficient 
R&D, technological improvements/advancement is not possible.  The Committee, 
therefore, recommends that R&D facilities should be improved an d its funding 
should also be enhanced. The Ministry of Heavy Industries has 
centers/autonomous bodies like Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI) 
and National Automotive Testing and R&D Infrastructure Project (NATRIP) for 
R&D of Internal Combustio n Engine (ICE) Vehicles. The Committee recommends 
that MHI should set -up R&D Centers for supporting EVs also for technological 
advancement.                                                                                               (Para 89) 

 20 
 
Action Taken Replies 
Noted. NATRIP is one of the most significant initiatives of the Govt. of India for 
the growth of Automobile sector in India and includes setting up of "State of the 
Art" automotive Homogenization, Testing, Certification and R&D infrastructure at 
three new centers at GARC, Chennai, NATRAX Indore, NIAIMT Silchar and 
upgradation of three existing centers at ARAI Pune, VRDE Ahmadnagar and 
ICAT Manesar (Gurugram).  
These centers supports EV for technical advancement. 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation  
 
The Committee is not satisfied with the response of the Ministry and 
reiterates its recommendation that budgetary allocation towards R&D should 
be significantly enhanced. The Committee desires that the Ministry should 
formulate policy for development of  Industrial parks for manufacturing EV 
components and their repairs, promote setting up of state -of-the-art R&D 
facilities for technological advancement of Electric Vehicles  and organising 
training of Automobile engineers in the field of EVs . The Committee should 
also be apprised of the steps taken to increase the funding for R&D. 
 
Recommendation/ Observation 
34. Some of the Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) informed the 
Committee that they made a great progress in localizing major components. 
However, few child parts are still imported from other countries like China. The 
import duties have been increased from 5% to 15% to encourage local 
manufactures. But due to non -production of some of the child -parts/components, 
the cost of Production has increase d due to hike in import duties. The Committee, 
therefore, recommends that Import duty may be raised only in a phased manner 
till such components are manufactured locally. 
(Para 94) 
 
Action Taken Replies 
The rate changes for the various parts of EVs were made in accordance with the 
Phased Manufacturing Programme notified by the Ministry of Heavy Industries 
vide notification No. 12(31)/2017-AEI dated 06.03.2019. 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
 
The Committee notes that even though the Ministry has fixed the 
import rate changes for the  various parts of EVs in accordance with the 
Phased Manufacturing Programme notified vide notification No. 12(31)/2017-
AEI dated 06.03.2019, the increase in import duty on certain child -
parts/components adversely affects the l ocal production cost. The Committee 
recommends that appropriate measures/ efforts should be made to keep the 

 21 
imported child-parts/components affordable along with providing impetus to 
local manufacturing.  
 
Recommendation/ Observation 
35. The Committee has been informed that at present EV Cars are taxed at 5%, 
and big Hybrid Electric Vehicles (HEVs) are taxed at 43% (28% GST plus 15% 
Cess). EVs reduce energy consumption by 75% over Internal Combustion Engine 
(ICE) while HEVs reduce energy consumption by 30 -45% over ICE without any 
external charger. Hence, HEVs are also entitled for discount on GST rate as in the 
case of EVs. GST support of HEV would help the whole eco -systems and provide 
impetus to EVs. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the GST rates on 
HEV may also be at a lower rate to create a lucrative EV ecosystem. 
(Para 100) 
 
Action Taken Replies  
The GST Council, at the time of initial fixation of GST rates, had discussed the 
issue of Compensation cess on hybrid vehicles in detail and recommende d that 
there may be no Compensation cess on small hybrid petrol cars (of engine 
capacity upto 1200 CC) and small hybrid diesel cars (of engine capacity upto 1500 
CC), and to impose 15% Compensation cess on other hybrid cars (big hybrid 
electric vehicles). Further, it is also to mention that subsequent to roll out of GST, 
compensation cess has been increased on large Internal Combustion Engine(ICE) 
cars consequent to the recommendation of the GST Council in its meeting held on 
09.09.2017. However, the Counci l recommended that status -quo be maintained in 
GST/ cess rates on Hybrid vehicles. Hybrid cars enjoy an advantage of 2% to 7% 
compensation cess as compared to normal ICE cars. 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
 
The Committee finds the reply of  MHI  to be unsatisfactory as there is 
no mention of any measures  to reduce the GST and Cess on Hybrid Electric 
Vehicles ( HEVs). The Co mmittee fails to understand the  rationale behind 
levying the highest GST  rate of 28 % on HEV s which is equivalent to ICE 
vehicles. The Committee reiterates its recommendation that since  Hybrid 
Electric Vehicles (HEVs) help in reducing fossil fuel consumption and carbon 
emissions, the GST rates on HEV should be lowered so as to incentivise their 
adoption. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 22 
CHAPTER – IV 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH THE 
FINAL REPLIES OF THE MINISTRY ARE STILL AWAITED 
 
Recommendation/ Observation 
36.  The Committee recommends that the Government should ensure strict 
adherence of “Battery Waste Management Rules, 2020” by all stake holders, for 
management of various types of waste batteries including lithium -ion batteries. 
The Committee hopes that with the imposition of „Extended Producer 
Responsibility‟, producers of batteries would collect waste batteries, ensure its 
recycling and recovery of rare earth -metals and re -use recycled elements thereby 
promoting circular economy & minimizing the adverse impact on environment. 
(Para 44) 
Action Taken Replies 
The recommendation has been forwarded to MoEFCC. 
 
Recommendation/ Observation 
37. The Committee was informed that for a universal and uniform charging 
provisions at charging stations, the Bureau of Indian Standards along with the 
Department of Science and Technology, the Principal Scientific Adviser and NITI 
Aayog are on the role to stan dardize the adapters so that transferability and inter -
operability is possible. The Committee desires that it be apprised of the outcome of 
such strategies developed by BIS and other stakeholders. 
(Para 71 (iii)) 
Action Taken Replies 
The recommendation has been forwarded to NITI Aayog, DST and BIS. 
 
Recommendation/ Observation 
38. The Committee further recommends that expenditure incurred on setting up 
of charging stations may be brought under the ambit of CSR for a limited period 
of 2 -3 years.  Further, re newal energy may be used for powering the Public 
Charging Stations. 
(Para 71 (vi)) 
Action Taken Replies 
The recommendation has been sent to MoF for further necessary action as 
the subject matter i.e. expenditure incurred on setting up of charging stations may 
be brought under the ambit of CSR for a limited period of 2 -3 years pertains to 
MoF. Regard to CSR for charging stations, the corporate entities may plan  
expenditure as per the provisions of Companies (CSR Policy) Rules, 2014.  The 
recommendation regard ing renewal energy for powering the Public Charging 
Stations has been forwarded to MoP 
 
 
 
 

 23 
Recommendation/ Observation 
39. Accordingly, the Committee recommends that the Government needs to 
forge international partnerships to secure access to key minerals.   The 
Government may form consortium for joint research, investment pooling and 
development of battery technology and battery recycling.  Since India is already a 
global powerhouse in information technology, communication, digital 
technologies, an excellen t foundation may be set up for the development of 
cutting-edge battery management systems.   
(Para 78) 
Action Taken Replies 
The recommendation has been forwarded to Ministry of Mines. 
 
Recommendation/ Observation 
40. Home to some of the most polluted citie s on the earth, India is pivoting 
towards new -energy electric vehicles to clean up its toxic air. But with meager 
resources of lithium, the mineral essential to make batteries for electric vehicles, it 
is having to scout for resources overseas. India‟s EV production will rely heavily 
on imports from China of lithium chemicals used to make cathodes and b attery 
cells as China has a thriving lithium chemical, battery cathode, battery cell and

explore other sources of battery raw material like Lithium etc. rather than solely

materials. 
(Para 81) 
Action Taken Replies 
The recommendation has been forwarded to DST. 
 
Recommendation/ Observation 
41. The Committee also recommends that Government should ensure 
strengthening supply chain network, easy availability and accessibility to raw 
material and components for batteries, to promote EV adoption. 
(Para 83) 
Action Taken Replies 
The recommendation has been forwarded to Ministry of Mines. 
  
Recommendation/ Observation 
42. The Committee notes that currently, loans for Internal Combustion Engine 
(ICE) vehicles are relatively easy to get with lower interest rates as the vehicle‟s 
value is well -understood, making loans secure for the bank. However, this is not 
the case with E Vs, as their residual value is not clear. The Committee, therefore, 
recommends that Government should designate EV as a priority lending sector, 
especially financing for commercial fleets, as they are critical to the transition 
towards cleaner mobility. Availability of easy loans with lower interest and longer 
tenures will make it easier for the consumer to go for EVs, which ultimately lead 
to faster adoption of electric mobility across the country.                          (Para 85)  

 24 
 
Action Taken Replies 
The recommendation has been forwarded to DoR. Further, the matter   
forwarded to MoF as DoR informed that it does not pertains to DoR.  
 
Recommendation/ Observation 
43. The aggressive push by the Government and EV manufacturers will 
certainly see a massive EV Industry setup in the coming years, including battery 
production, EV specific assembly lines as well as the charging infrastructure.  
This would naturally lead to a huge demand of technically skilled workforce in the 
area, as several auto makers have al ready announced their upcoming EV plans in 
the country. Meeting this demand will not be possible without the cooperation of 
the training institutes in the country. The Committee, therefore, recommends that 
EV-specific trainings/courses should be included i nto the curriculum of premier 
institutes like IITs, Engineering Colleges etc. to ensure that there is no scarcity of

(Para 96) 
 
Action Taken Replies 
The recommendation has been forwarded to NITI Aayog.

Recommendation/Observation 
1. The Committee notes that for the Financial Year 2022 -23, the M/o 
MSME has been allocated Rs. 21422 crore as BE against the projection of 
Rs. 24979.6  crore which translates to 85.76%.  Therefore, there is a 
shortfall of Rs. 3557.6 crore in BE allocation.  The SME division has been 
allocated Rs. 200 crore against the demanded amount of Rs. 208 crore, 
which comes to 96.15%.  However, the Committee notes that allocation to 
both DC -MSME and ARI Division of t he Ministry has been curtailed 
substantially as DC -MSME has got 88.99% whereas ARI Division got only 
72.73% of the projected amount.  Both ARI Division and O/o DC-MSME are 
the backbone of the Ministry of MSME and are therefore crucial for 
development and g rowth of MSME sector. The Committee understands that 
O/o DC -MSME implements policies and various programmes/schemes for 
providing infrastructure and support services to MSMEs whereas ARI 
Division looks after the administration of KVIC, COIR Board, MGIRI, 
besides supervising flagship schemes of the Ministry such as PMEGP, 
SFURUTI, ASPIRE, etc.  Therefore, inadequate allocation of funds would 
jeopardize the smooth functioning of the Ministry and successful 
implementation of its schemes/projects.  The Committe e, therefore, 
recommends that the M/o MSME should impress upon the Ministry of 
Finance to get enhanced budget allocation for both ARI Division and O/o 
DC-MSME at RE stage. 
(Para 9) 
Action Taken Replies 
The Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance, wh ile 
conveying approval of the Cabinet regarding continuation of Centrally 
Sponsored Schemes and Central Sector Schemes over the 15 th Finance 
Commission cycle i.e, FY 2021-22 to 2025-26, approved for continuation of  
SFURTI up to 30.09.2022 only. The proposal for budget enhancement under 
RE 2022 -23 will accordingly be taken up with the Ministry of Finance in 
view of the continuation of the scheme beyond 30.9.2022.

4.         PMEGP is one of the flagship Schemes of the Ministry of MSME, 
which is capable of gener ating large -scale employment for youth of the 
country, especially at this time of scarcity of employment in the country as a 
consequence of the Pandemic. The Committee, therefore, recommends that 
Ministry should ask for more allocations at the RE stage for  effective 
implementation of the Scheme in order to create large -scale employment for 
the workforce of the country. 
(Para 49) 
Action Taken Replies 
Ministry of MSME, through Khadi and Village Industries 
Commission (KVIC), is implementing PMEGP for generatin g self 
employment opportunities in the country by setting up micro -enterprises in 
non-farm sector.          
           Budget allocated for PMEGP for the FY 2022 -23(BE) is Rs.2500.00

Recommendation/Observation 
5.  The Commit tee observes that the ISEC issued and bank finance 
provided to the Institutions is yet to reach its full potential. The Committee, 
therefore, recommends that remedial measures should be taken by the 
Ministry to address the issues and create awareness drive  through various 
available modes to popularize the Scheme to increase the off take.  The 
procedures may be simplified, formalities may be kept at minimum, and 
banks may be educated about the Scheme and advised to adopt friendly and 
favourable approach while considering the applications and claims. 
(Para 59) 
Action Taken Replies 
As recommended by the committee, KVIC will request all the 
convenor of the State Level Bankers Committee (SLBC) to place the ISEC 
matter as one of the agenda point in their meetings in which the officer of 
the KVIC will explain about the scheme guidelines to make awareness 
among all the bankers for popularizing the ISEC scheme. 
          In order to simplify the procedures and minimize the formalities in 
the processing of ISEC claims,  KVIC has introduced an online portal to 
ensure timely settlement ISEC claims of KIs in a transparent manner. 
Recommendation/Observation 
6. The Committee notes that the BE for SFURTI Scheme for FY 2022 -
23is Rs. 334 crore but the Actual Expenditure as on 31 .02.2022 is Rs.

such an important scheme, whi ch is capable of generating employment in a

that budget earmarked for SFURTI scheme are utilized quarterly and 
planned manner and exhausted fully for effective implementation of the 
scheme in rural areas for benefit of the traditional artisans. 
(Para 63)

8. The Committee notes that export performance of coir and coir 
products during 2019-20 was not encouraging due to Covid Pandemic and 
consequent lockdowns but thereafter in 2020 -21, the targets were ach ieved 
by Coir Board. The Committee appreciates the efforts made by Coir Board 

 8 
in restoring the performance and display of resilience.  The Committee 
recommends that a contingency plan and strategy should be devised by Coir 
Board in order to tackle such unf oreseen situations like Covid pandemic in 
order to shield the Coir Sector from disaster as witnessed during 2019 -20. 
Further, the Committee recommends that high targets for exports should be 
set and endeavour should be made to achieve those targets by effe ctive 
planning and execution. Latest technology and techniques should be adopted 
for making coir products more competitive to meet the international 
standards. 
(Para 71)

assistance under the International Cooperation Scheme.  
 Organise networking & Product Promotion while participation in 
fairs.  
 Conduct International Buyer Seller Meets, both physical & virtual. 
 Sponsoring trade related and industry related delegations.  
 Exploration of virgin markets.  
 Undertake erosion control/soil stabilization projects using coir geo 
textiles. 
 Connect and coordinate the exporters, port authorities and 
logistical supports to boost exports. 
 Project the effectiveness of coir products in reversing global 
warming. 
 Display of products through Indian Council for Cultural Relation in 
Indian Missions abroad. 
 Increase the number of exporters by conducting awarenes s 
progremmes.

9. The Committee notes that during the Covid -induced lockdowns, 
MSMEs were adversely a ffected due to the shortage of raw material and 
their businesses incurred losses. The Committee, therefore, recommends that 
a robust procurement system should be evolved, which could ensure 
unhindered and timely supply of raw materials to MSMEs at reasonab le 
prices so that there is no scarcity of raw material supply to MSMEs. The 
Committee is also of the view that the Ministry should also explore other 
available options for raw material supply to MSMEs instead of becoming 
solely dependent on NSIC in coordin ation with other concerned 
Ministries/Departments to meet the requirement of MSMEs. 
 
(Para 73) 
Action Taken Replies  
Raw Material Storage Facility & Marketing Outlets are permissible 
under ID Project component of MSE-CDP. 

 10 
      National Small Industries Co rporation Limited (NSIC), a Public Sector 
Undertaking under this Ministry, facilitates Micro, Small and Medium 
Enterprises (MSMEs) to meet their raw material requirement by making 
arrangements with bulk manufacturers for procuring the materials and 
supplying the same to MSMEs. 
 
        KVIC is supplying the required Raw Material i.e Sliver/ Roving 
through its Departmental CSPs to the KIs. The required Cotton for CSPs is 
being procured from Cotton Corporation of India (CCI) to ensure good 
quality of Raw Mate rial and transparency. In addition to this, some of the 
KIs are having In-house pre-processing units/ conversion facility to convert 
the cotton into sliver/Roving. The CSPs and the pre -processing units are 
ensuring unhindered and timely supply of Raw Material to the KIs. 
         As regards to supply of raw material at reasonable price is concerned, 
it is to inform that, though there is a steep increase in cost of cotton, the 
price of Sliver/Roving of CSPs has not been increased and the price 
difference shall be met from the Price Fluctuation Fund available with CSPs 
As far as Coir Industry is concerned, the coconut husk is the basic 
raw material of industry for manufacturing variety of value added products 
out of coir. Coconut husks are abundantly available  in the coconut 
producing States of country. Coir Board is taking various efforts to ensure 
availability of the required quantity of coconut husks to coir manufactures 
in the MSME sector. The Coir Board has already addressed the State 
Governments of major coconut growing States where the coconuts husks 
are abundantly available, to incorporate necessary provision for husk 
collection in their industrial policies. The Board is also encouraging and 
supporting the MSMEs in the coir sector for establishment of hu sk 
collection centres and raw -material banks for ensuring easy availability of 
the raw -materials to the manufactures and thereby increasing the husk 
utilization of coir industry. As  the coconut husk are used as fuel in certain 
areas, the Board has been ad dressing the Governments of coconut 
producing states for taking appropriate action to ban the usage of coconut 
husk as fuel by introducing mandatory provisions. Further, in order to 
address the financial difficulties faced by the coir units for procurement s of 
raw materials, the Board has been supporting such entrepreneurs for setting 

 11 
up husk collection units through the various schemes being implemented by 
the Board like PMEGP, SFURTI, Mahila Coir Yojana, etc.  
NSIC facilitates MSMEs to meet their raw mate rial requirement like 
Iron & Steel, Aluminum, Paraffin wax, Bitumen, Emulsion, and Cement 
etc. by making arrangements with bulk manufacturers for procuring the 
materials and supplying the same to MSMEs. NSIC also provides financial 
assistance to MSMEs unde r their Raw Material Assistance (RMA) Scheme 
against bank guarantee for payment to the suppliers. The issue of regular 
increase in prices of raw materials specifically post Pandemic was regularly 
taken up by NSIC with the bulk producers. NSIC does not have  any direct 
control on the prices of raw material sold by PSUs & Private Manufacturers 
and final decision on prices is taken by the Manufacturers themselves. 
However, NSIC has made several communications and held meetings with 
Bulk suppliers of Steel, Alum inum i.e. SAIL, RINL & NALCO regarding 
steep hike in Steel & Aluminum prices and persuade them to have some 
check on the price hike. NSIC is making every possible effort in this regard 
and approaching private big Suppliers of Iron & Steel to have price 
advantage for MSME sector.  
 
Recommendation/Observation 
10.  The Committee observes that under National SC/ST Hub, the Actual 
Expenditure often has been less than the BE & RE. The Committee is 
concerned about the under -utilization of allocated funds meant for  the 
marginalized communities of the society. The Committee recommends that 
Ministry should endeavor to improve the situation by ensuring that the 
budget earmarked for SC/ST Hub Scheme is utilized fully for the intended 
beneficiaries. Lack of awareness amo ng the SC/ST entrepreneurs may be 
one of the main reasons for lower availment of various benefits offered 
under the scheme, hence efforts may be made to create awareness among 
SC/ST entrepreneurs through various available modes like print or social 
media e tc. Handholding of SC/ST entrepreneurs may work well in 
improving the performance of this scheme. Underutilization of funds is a 
serious cause of concern for the Committee; therefore, Ministry is advised 
to ensure full utilization of funds. 
(Para 79) 
 
 

 12 
Action Taken Replies 
  Under National SC -ST Hub, a number of initiatives have been 
introduced for providing support to the SC/ST entrepreneurs for capacity 
building and making them competitive. Various awareness campaigns 
through electronic media, newspapers,  etc. have been done for wider 
outreach of the scheme. Scroll message on NSSH scheme has been run on 
“DD national channel” to connect with SC -ST community across the 
country. Further for adequate awareness generation of National SC-ST Hub, 
extensive networ k of CSC -VLEs and Post Offices is being leveraged. 
Posters of NSSH scheme have been displayed at 5000 CSC-VLEs and 9178 
Post Offices across the country. In SC -ST predominant geographical areas, 
500 Nukkad Nataks have been conducted for creating awareness o n NSSH 
scheme. Awareness is also being created regularly through social media and 
also engaged key stakeholders such as Banks, CPSEs, EPCs, Training 
institutes etc. for last mile impact.  
Further, under the revised guidelines of the Scheme issued on 
15.11.2021, service sector has been included and now all the SC/ST MSEs 
of manufacturing as well as service sector are eligible for 25% subsidy under 
SCLCSS. In addition, provision  of assistance for participation in virtual 
exhibitions, assistance for registration in Government promoted e-commerce 
portal have been added.  The existing scale of assistance under various 
interventions of NSSH has also been increased. With the above initiatives, it 
is expected that more  SC/ST entrepreneurs will avail the benefits of 
NSSH and the entire fund allocated under the scheme  in BE 2022-23 will be 
utilised.  
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
11. The Committee noticed that overall credit gap in the MSME Sector is 
in the range of Rs. 20 lakh crore to Rs. 25 lakh crore.  The Committee  
observes that MSME Sector holds the key to make the Nation an economic 
superpower and MSMEs are critical to unlocking the potential of India

 KVIC roped in 4 Khadi Institutions  from Varanasi & Ghazipur 
districts in Uttar Pradesh for processing Raw Pashmina wool and 
weaving it further into woollen fabric. These institutions started 
procuring raw Pashmina wool from Leh -Ladakh, processing it in 
Delhi and further sending it back to Pashmina artisans in Leh - 
Ladakh for spinning. The Pashmina yarn was then brought to 
Varanasi for weaving. 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
 
The Committee notes that the Ministry is silent on the initiatives 
undertaken by KVIC in Aspirational Districts o f the country for 
promotion of  livelihood and employment opportunities to the rural 
artisans in the country .  The Committee, therefore, reiterates that the 

 47 
Ministry should take steps for enhancing the employment opportunities 
to the rural hinterland artisa ns in the country, especially in the 
Aspirational Districts on priority to ensure an equitable development 
throughout the length and breadth of the country. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
31. The Committee is concerned to note that out of the total number of 
applications received under the Scheme, around 36% of the total 
applications were rejected by the banks, only 25% of the applications got 
sanctioned by the banks and a meager 18% of applications got 
disbursements by the banks. Since PMEGP Scheme is one of the flagship 
Schemes of the Ministry, the Committee recommends that the Ministry 
should look into the matter and take steps for removing the hindrances and 
simplify the procedures with minimal formalities and technicalities so as to 
ensure that off take of loan under the scheme is improved. 
 
(Para 50) 
Action Taken Replies

 The Committee expresess  concern on the high rejection rate of 
applications by banks ( i.e. 50.4%),  which means half  of the 
applications received are being rejected under PMEGP Scheme.  The 
PMEGP Scheme is a flagship Scheme of the Ministry, which aims to 
generate employment opportunities in rural as well as urban areas of 
the country through setting up of new self -employment 
ventures/projects/micro enterprises. Therefore, t he Committee desires 
to know the reasons behind such high rejection rate by the banks . The 
Committee, therefore, recommends that remedial action  should be 
taken by the Ministry in consultation/co -ordination with the banks,  at 
the earliest, to remove the hurdles affecting proper implementation the 
Scheme. The Committee also recommends  to ease the procedure of 
availing loans for the applicants so that maximum number of applicants 
may avail the loans  under the Scheme. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
32. The Committee observes that the actual Interest Subsidy Eligibility 
Certificates issued and funds re leased by Banks are not very encouraging 
and creates gap in working capital requirement and actual fund availability 
as a result of which the Khadi Institutions fail to achieve the desired level of 
performance.  It has been brought to the notice of the Com mittee time and 
again that KVIC and banks are adopting a different working capital 
formula.  KVIC is assessing the recycling of working capital (working cycle) 
@ 16 months but on the other hand the banks are calculating it at 4 months 
and this is the bone of contention between KVIC and banks, which appears 
to be one of the lacunae for the gap existing between ISEC issued and Bank 
finance.  The Committee observes that this issue needs to be addressed at the 

 50 
appropriate level.  The Committee strongly recommen ds that an amicable 
formula may be devised by KVIC and banks, which is acceptable to both in 
order to increase the efficiency and efficacy of the ISEC scheme. 
 
(Para 58) 
Action Taken Replies 
 
The Chief Advisor (Cost), Ministry of Finance, Govt. of India ha s 
conducted the study to ascertain an appropriate Working Capital Formula for 
ISEC Scheme. The study report has been placed in the consultation meeting 
conducted with the representatives of major Khadi institutions/federations 
and other stake holders of Kh adi programme. Keeping in view of the 
decentralized nature of Khadi activities, the representatives of Khadi 
institutions/federations present in the meeting unanimously opposed for 
shortening down the operating cycle of Working Capital for Khadi 
programme and to retain the existing Working Capital Formula of KVIC. 
They further suggested conducting the study considering the peculiarities of 
working condition/decentralized nature of activities of Khadi sector. 
Subsequently, the subject matter has also been di scussed with the 
Bankers Meeting and Bankers were of the view that the KVIC‟s Working 
Capital formula should be modified/ brought down for acceptance of 
banking norms. 
Further, as per the recommendation, an internal committee has been 
constituted to study the existing Working Capital formula and to recommend 
for unanimous/ common working capital formula acceptable to the banks 
and study is under the way. On receipt of the study report the instant task 
may be assigned to the professional institute for furthe r practical study 
thereupon. 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
The Committee expresses displeasure on the poor performance of 
ISEC Scheme due to non -availability of working capital and 
understands that the issue which has been pending for a long time has  
not been resolved even after a series of meetings and study reports.  The 
Committee has time and again recommend ed to b ring an acceptable 

 51 
solution to both the Banks and KVIC on this issue but it seems there is 
inevitable delay on the part of Ministry of M SME and Ministry of 
Finance.  The Committee, therefore, express es strong displeasure and 
recommends that the matter may be resolved without any further delay. 
 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
33. The Livelihood Business Incubators (LBI), Technology Business 
Incubators (TBI) and Technology Centers under NSIC have been a source of 
employment for youth of the country. Further, NSIC through its Incubation 
Centres provides training to the prospective entrepreneurs in the 
manufacturing as well as service sector for skill development and 
employment purposes. The Committee recommends that more 
LBIs/TBIs/Incubation Centres should be established in cooperation with 
State Governments so that training on conventional as well as hi -tech trades 
are imparted to entrepreneurs for their skill development in areas of 
business operation for their gainful employment. 
(Para 74) 
 
Action Taken Replies 
 
ASPIRE Scheme has been approved for continuation from 2021 -22 to 
2025-26 with total budget outlay of Rs.194.87 crores.  As per the revi sed 
guidelines, the TBI component under ASPIRE scheme has been withdrawn 
owing to convergence with the Incubation Scheme of the Ministry. A 
network of 125 LBIs will be set up over the next 5 years with primary focus 
on providing incubation programs along w ith support services for formal 
micro-enterprise creation and imparting skill development programs for 
creating self and wage employment opportunities.  
 
In so far as NSIC is concerned, the Corporation is operating 7 LBIs at 
Deoria (Uttar Pradesh), Naini ( Uttar Pradesh), Kashipur (Uttarakhand), 
Nawada (Bihar), Rajkot (Gujarat), Chennai (Tamil Nadu) and Neemka 
(Haryana) which were established under ASPIRE scheme of Ministry of 
MSME. Further, LBI at Rourkela (Odisha) is currently under 
establishment. In addit ion, 4 Incubation Centres at Okhla (New Delhi), 
Howrah (West Bengal), Guwahati (Assam) and Mandi (Himachal Pradesh) 
are being operated by NSIC. 

 52 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
  
The Committee is not happy with the reply of the Ministry as the 
pace of s etting up number of Livelihood Business Incubators (LBI) has 
not increased as recommended by the Committee earlier.  The 
Committee is also aware that the Technology Business Incubators (TBI) 
component under ASPIRE Scheme has been withdrawn due to 
convergence with the Incubation Scheme of the Ministry  of MSME.   
The LBI and TBI (now renamed as Incubation Centres ) are very 
important components to inculcate entrepreneureship.  The Committee, 
therefore, reiterates that the Ministry should take necessary steps to  
increase the number and pace of setting up of more LBIs and 
Incubation Centres in the country. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
34. The Committee recommends that a countrywide comprehensive study 
needs to be conducted on the adverse impact of Covid pandemic o n MSME 
Sector in order to devise action plan and strategy to shield and strengthen 
the MSME Sector. The findings of the report may also be shared with the 
Committee for perusal. 
 
(Para 97) 
Action Taken Replies 
 
The Ministry of MSME on 7 th September, 2021 h ad assigned a Study 
to Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) to assess the impact 
of change in MSME classification on the Sector. The terms of reference of 
the said study inter -alia also included assessment of losses suffered by 
MSME sector due to Covid-19 pandemic.   
The said study was based on the survey conducted by SIDBI taking a 
random sample pool comprising 1,029 MSMEs spread across the 20 States 
and 2 Union Territories. The report of the study submitted on 27 th January, 
2022, reveals tha t 67 percent of the respondent MSMEs were temporarily 
closed for upto a period of 3 months and more than 50 percent of the 
respondent units witnessed a decline of more than 25 percent in their 

 53 
revenues during the FY 2020 -21. Around 66 percent of the respon dents 
reported a decline in profitability on account of stable fixed costs and 
decline in revenue. The study reveals that around 65 percent of the MSMEs 
surveyed, have availed the benefits under Emergency Credit Line Guarantee 
Scheme and around 36 percent of the respondents (MSMEs) also availed 
loans under the Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small 
Enterprises scheme. 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
 
The Committee notes the Ministry while submitting the details of 
survey conducted by SIDBI on the impact of Covid on MSME furnished 
no details of remedial action plan and strategy to shield and strengthen 
the MSME Sector.  The Committee, therefore, reiterates that the M/o 
MSME should apprise the steps being taken to put in place an action 
plan and st rategy to shield and strengthen t he MSME to withstand 
adverse impact in future, similar to Covid-19 Pandemic. 
 

 54 
CHAPTER – IV 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH 
THE  
FINAL REPLIES OF THE MINISTRY ARE STILL AWAITED 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
35. The Committee finds that under Emergency Credit Line Guarantee 
Scheme, repayment period of 3 -4 years including moratorium period is a 
very short period for MSMEs, which are struggling to survive from the 
second wave of Covid -19. The Committee, therefor e, recommends that the 
repayment period should be extended upto 7 -8 years with at least 2 years of 
moratorium on principal amount. With respect to the interest, moratorium 
for interest from 01.03.2020 onwards should be announced by RBI. 
 
(Para 26) 
 
Action Taken Replies 
 
The Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme is administered by 
Department of Financial Services (DFS), Ministry of Finance. This Ministry 
is taking up this matter with DFS. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
36. During the course of Committee meeti ngs, Members had raised the 
issue of banks’ lukewarm and unfriendly response towards borrowers, which 
often deter them to approach the banks for loans.  The Committee 
recommends that banks should adopt a friendly and favourable approach 
towards borrowers a nd make them aware about various schemes available 
for availing loans.  Separate windows for facilitating MSMEs may also be 
introduced in the banks for facilitating entrepreneurs.  
(Para 51) 
 
 
 
 
 

 55 
Action Taken Replies 
 
The issue raised by the Committee come s under the Administrative 
domain of Department of  Financial Services (DFS), Ministry of Finance. 
This Ministry is taking up this matter with DFS. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
37. The Committee hopes that the Champions Scheme achieves its 
targeted purpose f or which it has been introduced and performs well and 
proves to be beneficial for the MSME Sector.  The Committee desires that 
Committee may be apprised of the guidelines and all the important details of 
the Champions Schemes after the approval is accorded for the same. 
(Para 84) 
 
Action Taken Replies 
  During the Financial Year 2021 -22 the MSME Sustainable (ZED), 
MSME Competitive (Lean), MSME Innovative (Incubation, Design, IPR 
and Digital MSME) were approved through Standing Finance Committee 
(SFC) during  2021-22 with a revised scheme i.e., MSME Champions 
Scheme. The guidelines are under different stages of formulation and 
approval.  One component i.e., MSME Innovative has been launched on 
10.03.2022. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
38. The Committee appreciat es the introduction of GECL Scheme, which 
aims to meet the liquidity demand of the MSMEs in this critical time of 
pandemic and it hopes that the GECL Scheme proves successful and 
beneficial for the intended beneficiaries for the overall strengthening of 
MSMEs.  The Committee recommends that all the formalities and 
procedures of the scheme may be kept simple and convenient for the MSMEs 
for increasing off take and provide full advantage of the scheme to them.  
The Committee desires that the details of all th e modalities, progress made 
and utilization of funds allocated under GECL Scheme should be furnished 
to the Committee for its perusal. 
(Para 89) 

 56 
Action Taken Replies 
The suggestion of the Committee has been noted. Further, the GECL 
/ Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme is administered by Department 
of  Financial Services (DFS), Ministry of Finance. This Ministry is taking up 
this matter with DFS and Committee will be apprised accordingly. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
39. The Committee observes that as per  the information available, RAMP 
is a multi-faceted initiative of the Government assisted by the World Bank to 
develop capacities of MSMEs with administrative, financial, infrastructural 
and  techno-managerial support, which is yet to be launched on the gr ound. 
The programme is expected to develop and upscale MSMEs at least in the 
focal States and MSME Associations are eagerly waiting for launching of 
the programme and capture the pay -offs. The Committee notes that a 
weakness of the programme may prove to b e reliance on Government 
machinery and agencies for implementation of planned interventions. These 
agencies and offices are already implementing the respective schemes and 
notwithstanding the handholding and capacity building by global experts, 
under the aegis of World Bank, scope for improvements may be limited. The 
Committee recommends that following global practices, MSME federations 
and stakeholders may also be involved in implementation of the programme 
components under guidance and supervision of the Government. The 
Committee further recommends that the information about the progress 
made and the modalities of the RAMP Scheme may also be furnished to the 
Committee for its perusal as and when these are available. 
(Para 102) 
Action Taken Replies 
         The Cabinet, in its meeting dated 30 th March 2022, has approved the 
RAMP scheme. The Ministry has been actively involving Industry 
Associations representing the MSME sector through consultative meetings 
at all stages, including the project preparation sta ge. The States, during the

Associations, MSME Federations etc.   These industry associations will also 
be as sisting the Government (Centre and State) in implementation of the 
RAMP programme. 
The progress of the RAMP project will be made available to the Committee.

THE RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS, WHICH HAVE 
BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE MINISTRY 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
1. The Committee further notes that the Ministry has be en able to utilize  
99.62 percentage of the reduced revised allocation of Rs.900 crore for the 
financial year 2020-21.  As regards the present financial year 2021-22, MHI 
could utilize Rs.952.66 crore out of the RE allocation of Rs.1181 crore upto 
31.01.2022, which is ony 80% of the RE, with little time left for utilizing the 
remaining 20%. The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Heavy 
Industries which oversees important CPSEs, Heavy Electrical Equipments 
and Auto Sector etc. should ensure that the en tire RE is fully utilized in the 
remaining period of the financial year and should  henceforth rationalize the 
expenditure spreading all through the year to avoid uneven spending. 
 (Para 9) 
Action Taken Replies 
Budget allocation of Rs.  Rs.995.27 crore was enhanced to Rs.1181.00 crore 
at RE stage, against which the actual expenditure was Rs.1177.98 crore 
which was 99.75% of the RE. The major portion of the Budget at RE stage 
was for FAME-India (Rs.800.00 cr.) and entire amount of Rs.800.00 cr. for 
FAME-India was incurred by the end of March, 2021. In order to ensure that 
ongoing projects/schemes/initiatives of the FAME India-II Scheme were not 
to be affected, the additional funds for FAME -India-II Scheme were 
obtained through Supplementary Demands for Grants.  
 
Recommendation/Observation 
2. As per the written submission of MHI, the Committee notes that fund 
allocated for DCAAI under BE for 2021-22 i.eRs. 15 crores was enhanced to 
Rs. 22 crores at the RE stage. However, it is observed that the utilization of 
the funds upto 10.02.2022 has fallen short and is only 77% of the allotted 

 3 
fund of Rs. 22 crores. It is unlikely that the entire balance of 23% fund will 
be utilized in the remaining one and a half month. The Committee therefore 
recommends that MHI should adopt a rationalised approach for distribution 
of expenditure uniformally throughout the year to avoid under -utilization of

29. The Committee is deeply concerned to note that the MHI has been 
allocated a meagr e amount of Rs 200.25 crore for Development of Capital 
Goods Sector, one of the important sectors,  against the projection of 498.75 
crore, which is less than 50% of the actual amount demanded by the 
Ministry. The Committee is of the view that the Capital Goods sector is of 
the strategic and economic importance due to its capability to boost growth 
in the manufacturing sector and the overall economy and emphasis should 
be laid on building a globally competitive, self -reliant and sustainable 
Capital Goods Sector. The Committee therefore feels that  there is an urgent 
need for creating an ecosystem for export promotion, investment, 
technology, automation and driving new sustainable solutions which is 
crucial for accelerating India’s growth trajectory and harne ssing the full 
potential. The Committee strongly believes that Capital Goods industry is 
one of the key pillars of the Production -Linked Incentives (PLIs) to boost 
manufacturing sector growth by leveraging the emerging opportunities and 
further boosting gr owth in the Indian economy. Since the BE 2022 -23 
allocations are less than even half of the projected amount of Rs. 498.75 
crore for the Development Capital Goods Sector,  the Committee is of the 
view that to cater to the needs of the entire Capital Goods industry across 
the country, the BE allocation of Rs 200.25 crore would not be adequate. 
The Committee, therefore, recommends that MHI should address the issue of 
huge curtailment of funds for Development of Capital Goods Sector and  
seek enhanced allocati on at RE stage  so as to promote the growth and 
development of the Capital  Goods  Sector.

REPORT 
 
 The Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) sector has emerged as a highly 
vibrant and dynamic sector of the Indian economy over the last five decades. It contributes 
significantly in the economic and social development of the country by fostering 
entrepreneurship and generating large employment opportunities at comparatively lower 
capital cost, next only to agriculture. The MSMEs are complementary to large industries a s 
ancillary units and  this sector contributes significantly in the inclusive industrial 
development of the country.  The MSMEs are widening their domain across sectors of the 
economy, producing diverse range of products and services to meet demands of domes tic as 
well as global markets. As informed by the Ministry of MSME, the MSME sector has 
contributed 27 per cent to GDP in the FY2020-21, 36 per cent to Manufacturing Output in 
the FY2020-21, second largest employer after agriculture with 6.34 crore MSMEs providing 
employment to 11.10 crore persons and contributed 45 per cent to Export in the FY2021-22. 
  
2. The MSMEs have been contributing significantly to  the expansion of entrepreneurial 
endeavors through business innovations. The MSMEs in India are also playing a crucial role 
by providing large employment opportunities at comparatively lower capital cost than large 
industries as well as through industrialization of rural & backward  areas, inter alia, reducing 
regional imbalances, assuring more equitable d istribution of  national income and  wealth. 
Besides, the Ministry is working towards an agenda of inclusive development, and has taken 
various initiatives and measures to ensure that demographically as well as geographically 
weaker sections are benefitted for their overall development. 
  
Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises 
 
3. The Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MSME) envisions a 
progressive MSME sector by promoting growth and development of the Sector, including 
Khadi, Village and  Coir Industries, in cooperation with concerned Ministries/Departments, 
State Governments and other Stakeholders, through providing support to existing 
enterprises, adopting cutting edge technologies and encouraging creation of new 
enterprises. A number of statutory and non-statutory bodies work under the aegis of the 
Ministry of MSME. These include the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) 
and the Coir Board besides National Small Industries Corporation (NSIC), National 
Institute for  Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (NIMSME) and Mahatma Gandhi 
Institute for Rural Industrialisation (MGIRI).   
 
  

2  
4. The Ministry of MSME runs various schemes aimed at financial assistance, 
technology assistance and upgradation, infrastructure development, skill development and 
training, enhancing competitiveness and market assistance of MSMEs. The major schemes 
of the Ministry of MSME are as under: 
 
(i) Prime Minister‟s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) 
(ii) Credit Guarantee Trust Fund For Micro and Small Enterprises(CGTMSE) - 
 Provision of Collateral Free Credit for MSMEs 
(iii) A Scheme for Promotion of Innovation, Rural Industries & Entrepreneurship 
 (ASPIRE) 
(iv) Entrepreneurship and Skill Development Programme (ESDP) 
(v) Scheme of Fund for Regeneration of Traditional Industries (SFURTI) 
(vi) Micro and Small Enterprises-Cluster Development Programme (MSE-CDP) 
(vii) Scheme for providing financial assistance to Khadi institutions under MPDA 
(viii) MSME Champions Scheme (erstwhile CLCS-TUS) 
(ix) Raising and Accelerating MSME Performance (RAMP) Scheme 
 
New Definition of MSME 
 
5. In accordance with the provision of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises 
Development (MSMED) Act, 2006, the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) are 
classified as below: 
(i) a micro enterprise, where the investment in plan t and machinery or equipment 
does  not exceed one crore rupees and turnover does not exceed five crore 
rupees; 
(ii) a small enterprise, where the investment in plant and machinery or equipment 
does  not exceed ten crore rupees and turnover does not exceed fifty crore 
rupees; and 
(iii) a medium enterprise, where the investment in plant and machinery or 
equipment  does not exceed fifty crore rupees and turnover does not exceed 
two hundred and fifty  crore rupees. 
 
6. The new classification has come into effect from 1st July, 2020. The earlier criteria 
of classification of MSMEs under MSMED Act, 2006 were based on investment in plant 
and machinery/equipment. It was different for manufacturing and service units. It was also  
very low in terms of financial limits. Since then , the economy has undergone significant  
changes. A revision in MSME criteria of classification was announced under Atma Nirbhar  
Bharat package on 13th May, 2020. This has been done in order to be realistic with time 

3  
and to establish an objective system of classification and to provide ease of doing business. 
The turnover with respect to exports will not be counted in the limits of turnover for any 
category of MSME units which will offer major relief to the exporters. 
 
7. The primary responsibility of promotion and development of MSMEs is of the State 
Governments. However, the Government of India, supplements efforts of the State 
Governments through various initiatives. The role of the Ministry of MSME and its 
organisations is to assist the States in their efforts to encourage entrepreneurship, 
employment and livelihood opportunities and enhance the competitiveness of MSMEs in  
the changed economic scenario. 
 
8. The Committee is of the view that the new classification of MSMEs would bring 
about positive changes in the MSME Sector including many benefits that will aid 
MSMEs to grow in size  by attracting investments and would generate more 
employment opportunities. In this regard, in the deposition by the Secretary, Ministry 
of MSME on 20.02.2023 before the Committee, it emerged that although the change in 
definition of MSMEs is for their benefit, however,  a study is required for sector-wise 
segregation of  the MSM Es. The Committee  recommends that the Minist ry should 
carry out a study for sector -wise segregation of  the MSMEs in order to ensure 
targeted distribution of budgetary allocation s which w ould facilitate development, 
expansion and growth of the MSME sector.  
 
Dream of Five Trillion Dollar Economy and the MSME Sector 
 
9.      To achieve the set target of becoming the $5 trillion economy by 2024, t he 
Government is implementing various schemes, programmes and initiatives for the 
promotion, development and enhancing the competiveness of MSME sector in the country. 
A number of recent initiatives have been taken to strengthen, support, finance , revive and 
reconstruct MSMEs such as:  
(i) Rs. 5 lakh crore Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS), for 
businesses, including MSMEs was announced as a part of Atma Nirbhar Bharat 
Package with initial guarantee coverage of Rs. 3 lakh crore on 13.05.2020 with 
validity of scheme up to 30.11.2020. Subsequently, this was extended with 
infusion of Rs. 1.5 lakh crore on 29.09.2021 with validity of scheme up to 
31.03.2022 and with infusion of Rs. 50,000 crore on 01.02.2022 with validity of 
scheme up to 31.03.2023.  
(ii) Rs. 50,000 crore equity infusion through Self Reliant India (SRI) Fund. This 
scheme has a provision of Rs.10,000 crore from Government of India and Rs. 

4  
40,000 cro re leverage through Private Equity/Venture Capital funds. This 
initiative is aimed at providing growth capital to the deserving and eligible units 
of MSME sector.  
(iii) Credit Guarantee Scheme for Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs), for providing 
collateral free loan up to a limit of Rs. 200 lakh to MSEs with guarantee coverage 
up to 85 per cent  for various categories of loans. Further, Budget 2023 -24, has 
announced the infusion of Rs. 9,000 crore in the corpus of CGTMSE to enable 
additional credit of Rs. 2.00 lakh crore with a reduced cost of credit.   
(iv) New revised criteria for classification of MSMEs. 
(v) No global tenders for procurement up to Rs. 200 crore. 
(vi) “Udyam Registration” for MSMEs, for Ease of Doing Business w.e.f. 1.7.2020 
(vii) Launching of an online Portal “Ch ampions” in June, 2020 to cover many aspects 
of e-governance including grievance redress and handholding of MSMEs. 
(viii) Inclusion of Retail and Wholesale traders as MSMEs w.e.f. 2.7. 2021. 
(ix) Non-tax benefits extended for 3 years in case of an upward change in sta tus of 
MSMEs. 
(x) Launch of Udyam Assist Platform on 11.1.2023 to bring Informal Micro 
Enterprises (IMEs) under the formal ambit for availing the benefits under Priority 
Sector Lending.  
(xi) The Ministry of MSME  vide Notification no. S.O. 5670(E) dated 9.11.2018, had 
made it mandatory for all Central Government Ministries/Departments/ CPSEs to 
procure at least 25  per cent of their annual procurement from MSEs, including 3  
per cent from MSEs owned by women entrepreneurs vis-a-vis the target of 25 per 
cent, Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) procured 34  per cent from Micro 
& Small Enterprises in 2022-23.  
(xii) Field offices of Ministry of MSME organize various awareness campaigns for 
UDYAM registration  and benefits of Go vernment schemes /programmes, in 
coordination with MSME/ Industry Departments of States/UTs concerned and 
other MSME stakeholders through physical workshops, social media, print media 
& electronic media for creating wide publicity for increasing participat ion from 
all stake holders.  
(xiii) To address the issue of delayed payment to MSMEs, RBI has issued guidelines 
for setting up and operating the Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS) 
to facilitate the financing of trade receivables of MSMEs from corporate and 
other buyers, includ ing government departments and P ublic Sector Undertakings 
(PSUs) through multiple financiers electronically. 
  

5  
10. The Committee welcomes the goal of the Government for making India a $5 
trillion economy by the Year 2024-25 and opines that the target can be achieved by 
growth and development of the MSME sector. As MSME sector is vital for fostering 
entrepreneurship and generating self -employment opportunities at comparatively 
lower capital cost  and are complementary to large indu stries as ancillary units , 
formulation of targeted policies in the areas of infrastructure development, 
technological upgradation and forward linkage s could help MSMEs to achieve their 
full potential and propel the Indian economy to a higher growth traject ory. The 
Committee recommends that Government need to play a proactive role in promoting 
MSME Sector by handholding the MSME s at the grassroots level and for this , a top 
down approach needs to be implemented right  down to the last tier of the MSME 
sector in letter, spirit and action.  In this regard, a roadmap should be devised to 
achieve the desired results.  
 
Demands for Grants (2023-24) 
 
11. While making presentation on the DFG (2023-24) (Demand No. 68) , the Secretary, 
Ministry of MSME gave an overview about the Ministry and informed the Committee that 
the MSME Sector is providing livelihood to around 11.10  crore people. The Ministry also 
apprised the Committee about the challenges in the MSME Sector viz. (i) Formalization and 
Inclusion; (ii) Access to f inance; (iii) Access to market ; (iv) Access to technology ; (v) 
Access to digitalization  (vi) Infrastructural bottlenecks  and (vii) Inadequate 
skilling/reskilling.  
 
12. The Ministry also highlighted Vision India @ 2047 with regard to the MSME Sector, 
viz. (i) bring in all MSMEs into the formal sector and ensure access to affordable credit; (ii)  
technology for all; (iii) create a sustainable and globally competitive KVI sector for 
generating gainful employment and sustainable livelihoods; (iv) enhance servi ce sector 
through capacity  building/skilling; (v) gender parity in entrepreneurship; and (vi) ensure 
access to  markets and enhance MSMEs  share of exports. 
 
13. Regarding the details of the Action Plan set for the Ministry for the FY2023-24, the 
Committee was informed by the Ministry that an amount of Rs. 22137.95 crore has been 
allocated for the year 2023 -24. The Committee was also informed about the following 
highlights of the Union Budget 2023-24 for the MSME Sector: 
 Assistance for traditi onal artisans and craftspeople through PM Vishwakarma 
Kaushal Samman (PM VIKAS) Scheme  
 Infusion of Rs. 9,000 crore in the corpus of Credit Guarantee for MSMEs

under Vivad se Vishwas  I – Relief for MSMEs initiative in case of non -executed

include payments made to such enterprises within the ambit of section 43B of the

and re-appropriation of funds was resorted to  at the revised estimates stage . Although 
the re -appropriation of  funds for some of the schemes were got approved through 
Standing Finance Committee (SFC) at the end of the financial year , but the funds  
remained unutilized.  The Committee is of the view that it is not a healthy sign and 
such practices should be avoided as far as possible in future. 
 
18. It was observed that the allocations for the FY2022-23 of the Ministry were 
either decreased or increased at the revised estimate stage, but the actual expenditure 
incurred is less than the Revised Estimate. The Committee is of the view that scheme-
wise estimation of fund requirement s should be carried out effectively and sincerel y 
well in advance to ensure that budget allocations are utilized optimally. 
 
19. The Committee notes that for the FY2022-23, the Ministry was allocated Rs. 
21422.00 crore which was reduced to  Rs. 15628.71 at the RE Stage and the A ctual 
Expenditure up to the 31st January, 2023  stands at only Rs. 11112.01 crore which is 
71.1 per cent of the RE allocation.  The Committee is of serious concern in this regard 
and would like to be apprised about the reasons for such low utilization of allocations. 
The Committee is of the view that the Ministry should take necessary steps to utilize 
the balance amount of 29 per cent during the remaining period of the financial year in 
consonance with the Financial Rules . The Ministry should henceforth  rationalize its 
expenditure throughout the year to avoid uneven spending during the last quarter of 
the financial year.  
 
20. The Committee notes that an allocation of Rs. 199.88  crore was made at RE 
stage for the SME Division for the FY  2022-23 and the Actual Expenditure up to the 
31st January, 2023 stands at Rs. 118.46 crore, which is only 59.26 per cent of the RE 
allocations. As regards to ARI Division, the  RE for the FY 2022-23 was Rs. 3321.46 
crore whereas the Actual Expenditure up to the 31st January, 2023 is Rs. 2664.31 
crore, which is 80.21 per cent  of the RE allocation. In  case of  Office of DC-
MSME also, the RE was Rs. 12152.37 crore and the Actual Expenditure up to the 31st 
January, 2023 is only Rs. 8329.24 crore which clearly shows that the  DC-MSME could 
utilize only 68 per cent  of the RE for FY 2022 -23. The Committee would like to be 
apprised about the reasons for such low utilization of the allocations made and 
suggests to the Ministry that a systematic expenditure pattern should be devised to 
streamline its expenditure in future.

21. The Committee notes that the BE for FY2023 -24 is Rs. 22137.95 crore, which is 
a slight increase from the BE of Rs. 21,422 crore for the FY2022 -23. Out of this , an 
allocation of Rs.  14,100 crore has been earmarked for  the Guaranteed Emergency 
Credit Line Scheme (GECL) and, only Rs. 8037.95 crore is left for various other

difficult for the Ministry to implement its various schemes  effectively in the present

ask for enhanced allocation at the RE Stage for proper implementation of its  flagship
